newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar locked in tight range vs yen in quiet Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Dollar locked in tight range vs yen in quiet Tokyo.

text.p: 0322 GMT TRADED HIGH/LOW AS OF 0300 GMT

The dollar was locked in a tight range against the yen at the Tokyo midday on Thursday amid a dearth of fresh factors, with Japan's current account data and a Japan-U.S. business council out of the way, dealers said.
Concerns over Japan's swelling trade surplus linger, but the market's focus is shifting to European currencies ahead of the Bank of England's decision on interest rates later in day.

"Japan's current account surplus did show a significant rise yesterday, but the dollar did not fall that much," a trust bank dealer said, adding that a fresh factor would be needed if the dollar is to make another test of the downside.
He added that the greenback's topside remained heavy due to exporter offers and profit-taking interest near 113 yen.
Dealers said there was talk of bids from public fund bodies near 112.50 yen. Some Japanese investors are also said to be placing bids on the downside, supporting the greenback.
They added that the market will be focusing on the Bank of England's announcement on interest rates expected at 1100 GMT.
